hypotheses.title: Chicoric Acid Shortens Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Administration of chicoric acid shortens lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The effect is dose-dependent and observable under standard culture conditions.
hypotheses.rationale: Chicoric acid is a reactive polyphenol that can generate oxidative stress and perturb mitochondrial function. Such biochemical stress may accelerate cellular damage and reduce organismal longevity.
hypotheses.prediction: Worms treated with chicoric acid will show a statistically significant reduction in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, expose them to multiple chicoric acid doses throughout adulthood, and compare survival curves with vehicle-treated controls using log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Sesamolin Extends Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Administration of sesamolin extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The effect is dose-dependent and observable under standard culture conditions.
hypotheses.rationale: Sesamolin is a lignan with antioxidant properties that can counteract accumulating oxidative damage. Reduced oxidative burden is a recognized route to slower aging and prolonged survival.
hypotheses.prediction: Worms treated with sesamolin will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, expose them to multiple sesamolin doses throughout adulthood, and compare survival curves with vehicle-treated controls using log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Phenelzine Sulfate Extends Lifespan in C. elegans
hypotheses.claim: Administration of phenelzine sulfate extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans. The effect is dose-dependent and observable under standard culture conditions.
hypotheses.rationale: Phenelzine sulfate is a monoamine oxidase inhibitor that alters amine metabolism and can influence stress-response signaling. Modulation of such conserved pathways is a plausible mechanism for extending longevity.
hypotheses.prediction: Worms treated with phenelzine sulfate will show a statistically significant increase in median and maximum lifespan compared with untreated controls.
hypotheses.experiment: Synchronize worm populations, expose them to multiple phenelzine sulfate doses throughout adulthood, and compare survival curves with vehicle-treated controls using log-rank analysis.

hypotheses.title: Chicoric Acid Extends Lifespan via DAF-2 Activation
hypotheses.claim: Administration of chicoric acid extends lifespan in Caenorhabditis elegans by activating the insulin/IGF-1 receptor DAF-2. The lifespan extension requires functional DAF-2 signaling.
hypotheses.rationale: DAF-2 is the central receptor of the insulin/IGF-1 signaling pathway that governs aging in C. elegans. Modulating this receptor can reprogram downstream FOXO-mediated transcription and alter longevity.
hypotheses.prediction: Chicoric acid will extend lifespan in wild-type worms but fail to extend lifespan in daf-2 loss-of-function mutants.
hypotheses.experiment: Compare survival curves of chicoric acid-treated wild-type and daf-2 mutant worms against their respective vehicle-treated controls under identical conditions.
